title: Days of the week
summary: Name the seven days of the week, say what day it is and join two nouns with the iḍāfa: يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَة.
intro: The Arab week starts on Sunday, and most day names come from numbers: الاِثْنَيْن (Monday) is 'the second' and الْخَمِيس (Thursday) 'the fifth'. The full name puts two nouns together: يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَة (the day of Friday). This noun + noun pattern is called the iḍāfa, Arabic's way of saying 'of'.
objectives: Say the seven days of the week in order
Ask and say what day it is today
Build 'the … of …' phrases with the iḍāfa

realLife.title: The new timetable
realLife.story: There is a new timetable on the notice board, and Daniel wants to know which days he has class. Layla explains the Egyptian week, and Sami invites Daniel to Friday lunch with his family.

sentences.en: I have a lesson on Sunday.
sentences.literal: at me (is) a lesson (on the) day (of) Sunday

mistakes.why: Day names always keep their الـ: al-aḥad, as-sabt, al-jumuʿa.
In an iḍāfa the first noun never takes الـ: kitābu Dānyāl.

sentences.en: Friday and Saturday are days off in Egypt.
sentences.literal: the Friday and the Saturday (are a) holiday in Egypt

dialogue.title: Which days do we have class?
dialogue.culture: In Egypt the working and school week runs from Sunday to Thursday, and the weekend is Friday and Saturday. Friday is the day of the big midday prayer, and many families eat a long lunch together after it.

lines.ar: يَا لَيْلَى، هٰذَا جَدْوَلُ الدُّرُوس الْجَدِيد. مَتَى عِنْدَنَا دَرْس؟
lines.en: Layla, this is the new class timetable. When do we have lessons?

lines.ar: عِنْدَنَا دَرْس كُلَّ يَوْم، مِنْ يَوْمِ الْأَحَد إِلَى يَوْمِ الْخَمِيس.
lines.en: We have a lesson every day, from Sunday to Thursday.

lines.ar: مِنَ الْأَحَد؟ فِي أَمْرِيكَا الْأُسْبُوع يَبْدَأُ يَوْمَ الاِثْنَيْن!
lines.en: From Sunday? In America the week starts on Monday!

lines.ar: وَفِي لُبْنَان أَيْضًا. لٰكِنْ فِي مِصْر الْجُمُعَة وَالسَّبْت عُطْلَة.
lines.en: In Lebanon too. But in Egypt, Friday and Saturday are days off.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا أَصْدِقَاء! مَا هٰذَا؟ هَلْ هٰذَا الْجَدْوَل الْجَدِيد؟
lines.en: Good morning, friends! What's this? Is this the new timetable?

lines.ar: نَعَم. يَا سَامِي، مَا الْيَوْم؟ هَلِ الْيَوْم يَوْمُ الاِثْنَيْن؟
lines.en: Yes. Sami, what day is it today? Is today Monday?

lines.ar: لَا، الْيَوْم يَوْمُ الثُّلَاثَاء، وَغَدًا يَوْمُ الْأَرْبِعَاء.
lines.en: No, today is Tuesday, and tomorrow is Wednesday.

lines.ar: الثُّلَاثَاء؟ إِذَنْ عِنْدَنَا دَرْسُ الْقِرَاءَة الْيَوْم، صَحِيح؟
lines.en: Tuesday? Then we have the reading lesson today, right?

lines.ar: صَحِيح، دَرْسُ الْقِرَاءَة يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاء وَيَوْمَ الْخَمِيس.
lines.en: That's right, the reading lesson is on Tuesday and on Thursday.

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة عِنْدَنَا غَدَاء كَبِير فِي بَيْتِ عَائِلَتِي. تَعَالَ!
lines.en: Daniel, on Friday we have a big lunch at my family's house. Come along!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا سَامِي! يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة أَنَا فِي الْبَيْت، لَا مُشْكِلَة.
lines.en: Thank you, Sami! On Friday I am at home, so no problem.

lines.ar: وَيَوْمَ السَّبْت؟ هَلْ عِنْدَكَ وَقْت يَا دَانْيَال؟ نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَتْحَف؟
lines.en: And on Saturday? Do you have time, Daniel? Shall we go to the museum?

lines.ar: فِكْرَة جَمِيلَة! السَّبْت يَوْم جَمِيل لِلْمَتْحَف.
lines.en: A lovely idea! Saturday is a nice day for the museum.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز! الْجُمُعَة مَعَ عَائِلَتِي، وَالسَّبْت فِي الْمَتْحَف. أُسْبُوع جَمِيل!
lines.en: Excellent! Friday with my family, and Saturday at the museum. What a lovely week!

reading.title: My week in Cairo
reading.ar: فِي الْأُسْبُوع سَبْعَة أَيَّام. أُسْبُوعِي فِي الْقَاهِرَة: مِنْ يَوْمِ الْأَحَد إِلَى يَوْمِ الْخَمِيس عِنْدِي دُرُوس فِي الْمَدْرَسَة. يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة أَنَا مَعَ عَائِلَةِ سَامِي. وَيَوْمَ السَّبْت أَنَا فِي الْمَتْحَف مَعَ لَيْلَى.
reading.en: There are seven days in a week. My week in Cairo: from Sunday to Thursday I have lessons at the school. On Friday I am with Sami's family. And on Saturday I am at the museum with Layla.

quiz.prompt: How do you say 'Friday' in full, as an iḍāfa?
In the dialogue, which days are days off in Egypt?
In السَّبْت the l of the article is not pronounced. Why?

completion: Excellent! You know the seven days of the week and can say 'the … of …' with the iḍāfa.
